repo: Closed source. Upstream evidence came from Cursor's own shipped runtime package: https://downloads.cursor.com/lab/2026.10.19-6bbf2c4/linux/x64/agent-cli-package.tar.gz (package.json name "@anysphere/agent-cli-runtime", version label 2026.10.19-6bbf2c4), obtained from the official installer https://cursor.com/install
surfaces:
1) cursor-agent CLI (binary name "cursor-agent", symlinked as "agent"; official install https://cursor.com/install -> ~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/<ver>/cursor-agent).
2) Cursor IDE "Agent" surface — the IDE uses the SAME agent runtime, so it writes the same agent-transcripts tree (Cursor staff: "Local IDE chats like agent-transcripts / editor index"; the IDE's .cursorignore allowlist in the upstream bundle contains "!projects/*/agent-transcripts/**" under the comment "Agent transcripts for citation").
3) ACP (Agent Client Protocol) surface — ~/.cursor/acp-sessions/<id>/{store.db,meta.json} (upstream ./src/acp/acp-storage.ts).
4) Legacy Cursor IDE "Composer" chat — %APPDATA%\Cursor\User\{globalStorage,workspaceStorage\*}\state.vscdb (SQLite KV), a SEPARATE store from the CLI (staff: "local IDE chats and CLI or SDK sessions live in different storage and don't sync").
binaries: cursor-agent (linux/darwin x64|arm64, and a Windows build) — single-file Node/Bun SEA bundle plus `cursor-agent-worker-sea`, `node`, `file_service.linux-x64-gnu.node`, and node_modules with better-sqlite3 12.11.1, tree-sitter-bash 0.21.0, piscina. Windows install equivalent is not published in the same tarball; the runtime honours %CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR% / %CURSOR_DATA_DIR% on win32 as well.

paths: %USERPROFILE%\.cursor\projects\<sanitized-workspace-path>\agent-transcripts\<conversationId>\<conversationId>.jsonl   ← RECOMMENDED PARSE TARGET (CLI + IDE agent transcripts)
%APPDATA%\Cursor\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb   (IDE composer store — SQLite KV table cursorDiskKV)

Root override: upstream resolves the config root as $CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR ?? $XDG_CONFIG_HOME\cursor ?? %USERPROFILE%\.cursor, and the projects root as $CURSOR_DATA_DIR ?? %USERPROFILE%\.cursor (upstream ../cursor-config/dist/paths.js, exports WI/Xq/kL/m4/ok/qA)
storage.format: ADAPTER TARGET = PLAIN JSONL (newline-delimited, one JSON object per line, UTF-8, no BOM, no compression). Line shape is role-nested Anthropic-ish: {"role":"user"|"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":...},{"type":"tool_use","name":...,"input":{...}}]}} plus a control line {"type":"turn_ended","status":"success"}. Older Cursor builds used two other shapes and all three are still seen in the wild: flat {"role","content"} and type-nested {"type":"user","message":{"role","content"}}. AUXILIARY (not needed for the adapter): chats/<md5>/<id>/store.db = SQLite (CREATE TABLE blobs(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, data BLOB); CREATE TABLE meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT); PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL) whose blobs are a content-addressed Merkle tree (tree blobs = protobuf frames, leaf blobs = JSON) and are ENCRYPTED with blobEncryptionKey, which is stored in the same meta row (key='0', hex-encoded JSON) — so they are locally decryptable but need real crypto work; IDE state.vscdb = plaintext SQLite key/value (table cursorDiskKV(key,value), keys composerData:<id> and bubbleId:<cid>:<bid>, bubble JSON carries toolFormerData{name,params,result,additionalData.status}).
storage.append_semantics: APPEND-ONLY AND LIVE for the JSONL target. Upstream TranscriptStore.writeFromStateIncremental uses fs.promises.appendFile for every write after the first; the first write of a session is a full writeFile; turn_ended is appended as its own line. Writes are serialised through a promise chain (enqueueWrite) so record order == chronological order. FALLBACK: upstream option fallbackToFullWriteOnIncrementalFailure defaults to true, so an append error triggers a FULL REWRITE of the file (writeFile) — the file can therefore shrink or be replaced wholesale. Cursor staff: "Writing transcripts to disk is not atomic. If the machine was slow and rebooted during a write, the files could end up empty or be lost." Discodex's existing LogTailer handles this: its `length < cursor.offset` branch resets the offset and re-reads from 0, which re-derives the correct final state. No watcher.rs change is required.
storage.session_file_naming: Conversation id = a UUID; it is simultaneously the agent-transcripts directory name, the file stem, the chats/<md5>/<id> child, and the acp-sessions/<id> directory. Canonical: agent-transcripts/<conversationId>/<conversationId>.jsonl. Legacy flat: agent-transcripts/<conversationId>.jsonl. Subagent: agent-transcripts/<parentId>/subagents/<childId>.jsonl (the parent link exists only in the path; the lines carry no ids). Project grouping: projects/<sanitized(workspacePath)>/ where sanitize() replaces every char outside [A-Za-z0-9] with '-', collapses runs of '-', and trims leading/trailing '-'; the chats store groups by md5(resolve(cwd)) instead. Long paths: if the project dir exceeds 91 chars it is truncated to 83 chars plus '-' plus the first 7 hex of sha256 (upstream kL).

fields.project: YES. (a) Best: infer from any absolute file path in a tool_use input via the existing detect_project_root() (finds .git/Cargo.toml/package.json/... walking up) — no extra reads, mirrors the Antigravity adapter. (b) Exact: chats/<md5(cwd)>/<id>/meta.json holds the absolute "cwd" in plain JSON (upstream ./src/state/chat-session-meta.ts) — needs a scan of chats/*/<id>/meta.json to map a transcript id to its bucket. (c) Lossy fallback: last '-' segment of the sanitized project dir. Only the final folder name is ever published.
fields.model: PARTIAL — NOT in the JSONL transcript. Available in the SQLite store: store.db meta row (key='0') holds lastUsedModel (e.g. "gpt-5.4-high"), verified upstream in the agent-kv metadata shape {agentId, latestRootBlobId, name, mode, isRunEverything, approvalMode, createdAt, lastUsedModel, ...}. Reaching it needs a SQLite reader (new rusqlite/better-sqlite3 dependency) + hex decode of the meta value. Cheap approximation without SQLite: %USERPROFILE%\.cursor\cli-config.json -> selectedModel.modelId (plain JSON) — but that is the globally selected model, not the session's.
fields.file_basename: YES. tool_use.input.path is the file argument for Read/Write/StrReplace/Delete (upstream Cursor dialect: path, not Claude's file_path). The existing extract_file_basename() already looks for the "path" key, so it works unmodified; language_from_file() then yields Rust/TypeScript/...
fields.tool_activity: YES. tool_use.name plus tool_use.input (an OBJECT, not a JSON string). Observed Cursor tool vocabulary: Read, ReadFile, Write, StrReplace, Edit, Delete, Grep, Glob, Shell, WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, ReadLints, SemanticSearch, CreatePlan, ApplyPatch, Task, AskQuestion, rg. Upstream Claude->Cursor tool-name map confirmed in the bundle: {Bash:"Shell", Read:"Read", Write:"Write", Edit:"Write", Grep:"Grep", WebFetch:"WebFetch", WebSearch:"WebSearch", Task:"Task"}. Shell's input carries "command" (+ cwd); Write's carries "contents"; StrReplace's carries "old_string"/"new_string". The existing classify_tool(name, command) can be reused but needs a Cursor-specific pre-map (e.g. "strreplace" does not match its edit patterns).
fields.phase: YES. role "user" = new turn (TaskStarted); role "assistant" with only a text part = Thinking; a tool_use part = ToolStarted (phase -> RunningTools); {"type":"turn_ended","status":"success"} = Completed. No tool_result records exist in the transcript, so ToolFinished must be synthesised at the next turn boundary (or use the untacked ToolStarted/ToolFinished pair rather than TrackedToolStarted, which needs a call id the transcript does not provide).
fields.timestamps: PARTIAL. The transcript carries NO per-record timestamp field upstream (measured: 5246 lines over 191 real files, message keys are only "content"; no id/model/usage/timestamp). The only in-band time is a "<timestamp>Sunday, Jul 26, 2026, 1:06 PM (UTC+3)</timestamp>" block prefixed to the user text — observed in real transcripts by deja-vu, but NOT found in the cursor-agent bundle, so it is very likely IDE-injected: treat as best-effort, never as authoritative. Reliable alternatives: chats/<md5>/<id>/meta.json createdAtMs/updatedAtMs (Unix ms, plain JSON), and the transcript file mtime (upstream's own listRecentConversationsFromDisk() uses stat().mtimeMs as lastUpdatedAt). Recommend TaskStarted.started_at_ms = parsed <timestamp> block, else meta.json createdAtMs, else the observation time (same fallback Claude Code uses).

parser_strategy:
parse_line_for(Provider::Cursor, line) — one line of the JSONL -> Vec<ParsedEvent>:

1) {"type":"turn_ended", ...}                     -> [Completed]            (status success|error|aborted; never forward "error")
2) {"type":"error", ...}                        -> []                     (never forward the message)
3) role == "user"                               -> [TaskStarted{ started_at_ms }]  (+ nothing else; the prompt text is NEVER forwarded)
4) role == "assistant", message.content[] parts:
     - {"type":"text","text":...}                -> Thinking{ reasoning: None }     (text is dropped; assistant text + thinking are merged into ONE text part upstream, so no reasoning is recoverable)
     - {"type":"tool_use","name":N,"input":I}    -> ToolStarted{ activity }  with a Cursor-specific builder:
         label  = cursor_label(N, I.command)    (pre-map: Read/ReadFile/ReadLints->"Reading project files"; Write/StrReplace/Edit/Delete/ApplyPatch->"Editing files"; Grep/Glob/rg/SemanticSearch->"Searching project"; WebSearch/WebFetch->"Browsing documentation"; TodoWrite/CreatePlan->"Planning changes"; Task/Subagent->"Running coding agent"; AskQuestion->"Waiting for input"; Shell -> delegate to the existing classify_tool(N, command) so "cargo test" -> "Running Rust tests")
         file   = basename(I.path)              (existing extract_file_basename already matches the "path" key)
         language = language_from_file(file)
       and, when I.path is absolute, ALSO SessionMetadata{ project, cwd } via the existing detect_project_root() (same mechanism the Antigravity adapter uses) — this is what supplies the project name and the Rust/TypeScript stack.
5) legacy shapes: {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."}} and {"role":"user","content":"..."} -> [TaskStarted]; "content" may be a string or a block array.

Subagents: when the transcript path is agent-transcripts/<parent>/subagents/<child>.jsonl, also emit SubagentSpawned{ conversation_id: <parent>, agent: "" } so state.rs links the child session to the parent (it matches on the path containing the id).

TaskStarted timestamp: parse the "<timestamp>...</timestamp>" block out of the FIRST user text (only at the start, only a locale-shaped match, cap the length) and convert with chrono; otherwise fall back to now_ms (events.rs's current_time_ms) — the same fallback Claude Code uses. Never forward the surrounding text.

Not emitted: TrackedToolStarted/TrackedToolFinished (the transcript's tool_use has NO id, so calls cannot be paired) and ToolFinished per tool (no tool_result in the transcript). Use the untacked ToolStarted, and synthesise ToolFinished on the next user turn (all tools of the previous turn are done by then), and Completed on turn_ended.

risks: Format churn is real and already observed: the JSONL line shape has changed at least three times across Cursor versions (flat {role,content} -> type-nested {type,message} -> role-nested {role,message.content[]}). The parser must accept all three and ignore anything else.

The upstream full-rewrite fallback (fallbackToFullWriteOnIncrementalFailure=true) can replace the whole transcript mid-session, and cursor-agent --resume has been reported to clobber a transcript. LogTailer handles the shrink case (offset reset + re-read), but the presence can briefly flicker; a per-file record-identity guard would remove that.

Writes are explicitly non-atomic (Cursor staff): a crash or reboot mid-write can leave a transcript empty or truncated. The adapter must treat an empty or malformed file as "no information" and never as an error state.

The <timestamp> block is the only in-band time and it is NOT part of the upstream CLI bundle, so it is probably IDE-injected and must be treated as best-effort; a user prompt can also contain a literal <timestamp> block, so only accept one at the very start of the first user text and validate the shape.

Tool results are absent from the transcript, so TrackedToolStarted/TrackedToolFinished cannot be used (no call id) and per-tool ToolFinished has to be synthesised at turn boundaries; a tool that never returns would leave the phase at "Running tools" until the next user turn.

The project folder name is lossy (every non-alphanumeric char becomes '-', runs collapse), so a workspace named "my-app" becomes "my-app" and the last-segment heuristic yields "app". Prefer detect_project_root() on absolute tool paths, or meta.json's cwd.

No per-session model id in the transcript; adding it means reading store.db, which is an encrypted-blob SQLite (blobEncryptionKey in the same meta row) and therefore pulls in a sqlite crate AND real crypto work — flag that cost before promising "model" parity with Codex/DSH.

IDE and CLI use different stores and different session id spaces, and Cursor staff says they do not sync and there is no shared stable id; one Discodex Provider::Cursor variant will therefore see IDE agent chats and CLI chats in the same presence stream, with no way to link them by id.

The IDE's classic composer chat lives in %APPDATA%\Cursor\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb (SQLite cursorDiskKV) and is NOT covered by the JSONL adapter; reading it needs a sqlite crate, and the bubble values embed full conversation text plus toolFormerData.result (raw tool output) — a much higher privacy risk than the transcript.

Long-path handling: upstream truncates the project dir to 83 chars + a 7-hex sha256 suffix past 91 chars, and falls back to %CURSOR_DATA_DIR% or even /tmp/.cursor if the projects root is very long — so a path-based match can miss the real project folder.
CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR / CURSOR_DATA_DIR can relocate the whole tree; the adapter must read them or it will silently find nothing on a configured machine.
confidence: High for the CLI/IDE agent-transcript path, format, record shapes and append semantics (verified directly against Cursor's own shipped runtime package 2026.10.19-6bbf2c4 and corroborated by Cursor staff forum statements). High for the IDE state.vscdb layout (schema + key names from two independent reverse-engineering projects, no upstream source available because the IDE is closed source). Medium for the <timestamp> block (observed in real transcripts by a third party but not present in the upstream CLI bundle). Low/UNVERIFIED for the sanitized project-dir spelling on Windows (upstream sanitiser preserves case and produces e.g. "C-Users-PC-Documents-Discodex"; third-party reports of a lower-cased drive letter ("d-1-Backend") were not reproducible from the upstream code).
summary: Cursor DOES write a local, plaintext, APPEND-ONLY JSONL activity log that Discodex can tail with the existing LogTailer, with no new Rust dependency. The cursor-agent CLI (and the Cursor IDE's agent surface, which shares the same runtime) writes one JSONL transcript per conversation at %USERPROFILE%\.cursor\projects\<sanitized-workspace-path>\agent-transcripts\<conversationId>\<conversationId>.jsonl, appending one record per line as the agent works, and appending {"type":"turn_ended","status":"success"} at the end of a turn. Every record needed for rich presence is recoverable WITHOUT shipping conversation text: the tool_use blocks carry the tool name and its input object, so the current file basename (input.path), the normalized tool activity (Read/Write/StrReplace/Shell/Grep/... plus input.command) and the project (absolute path -> detect_project_root, or chats/<md5(cwd)>/<id>/meta.json "cwd") are all available; role=user/assistant plus turn_ended give the phase and the turn boundary, and the task start time comes from the "<timestamp>" block or meta.json createdAtMs / file mtime. Two gaps, both explicit: (1) the model id is NOT in the transcript — it lives in store.db's meta row (lastUsedModel), i.e. SQLite with ENCRYPTED content-addressed blobs, so a model label needs a sqlite crate plus crypto work, or the global cli-config.json selectedModel.modelId as an approximation; (2) tool RESULTS are absent from the transcript (they live only in store.db), so TrackedToolStarted/TrackedToolFinished (call-id based) cannot be used and ToolFinished must be synthesized at the next turn boundary. The IDE's classic composer chat is a different store entirely: %APPDATA%\Cursor\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb, a SQLite key/value table cursorDiskKV whose bubble values carry toolFormerData{name,params,result} — parseable, but it needs a sqlite crate (new dependency) and it is a rewritten blob file, not a tailable log, so it is out of scope for the watcher. Verdict: rich, via the agent-transcripts JSONL only.
